title: Shadow-validation-driven kernel switchover for mixed-precision paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a runtime kernel switchover mechanism that enables safe, measurable migration of requests to lower-precision execution paths (INT8/FP8) while preserving customer-facing quality. The system will use a shadow-execution validation pipeline that runs candidate low-precision kernels in parallel (shadow) and continuously compares outputs against the production FP16 path. Decisions to promote a quantized path (partial or full traffic) will be gated on defined accuracy metrics evaluated on live traffic and calibration suites.

Why:
- Quantized paths (INT8/FP8) provide substantial unit-cost reductions but can introduce subtle accuracy regressions on some prompts or models.
- Past rollouts were manual, slow, and required heavy offline calibration. We need an automated runtime guardrail to accelerate safe adoption of quantized kernels.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Accurate shadow validation that catches regressions before exposure: top-k agreement and embedding similarity thresholds satisfied for 99% of samples on the calibration set.
- Allow automated canary promotions when shadow validation passes for a rolling window (default 24h).
- Production performance: p95 latency regression of promoted path <= +5% vs FP16 baseline under same batching.
- Cost saving target: >=20% token cost reduction for promoted traffic.
- Reliable rollback: any alert on quality or latency triggers immediate traffic failover to FP16.

Design (high level):
1) Quantization profile catalog: persisted calibration artifacts per model version (INT8/FP8 profiles, per-layer scales, bias correction factors) produced by offline calibration jobs and surfaced to runtime.
2) Switchover policy engine: policy config that considers model version, sequence length bucket, quant profile, historical shadow delta metrics, customer tier and latency SLOs. Policies are JSON-configurable via Console.
3) Shadow executor: for a sampled subset of requests, run the candidate quantized kernel in shadow mode (no effect on response path), capture outputs and telemetry (latency, memory, top-k logits, embeddings). Shadow sampling rate is configurable; default 1%.
4) Accuracy validator: streaming comparator that computes metrics: top-1/top-5 agreement, KL divergence on logits, embedding cosine similarity, generation token-level disagreement rate, and task-specific metrics (e.g., answer correctness where ground truth exists). Uses rolling windows and stratified aggregation (by route/model/seq-len).
5) Promotion controller: promotes a quantized path to canary (e.g., 1% traffic) when shadow metrics meet thresholds for X hours and SLOs remain within budget. Promotions are timeboxed and require health checks.
6) Rollback & safety nets: automatic rollback if metric regressions exceed thresholds or if latency/cpu/gpu resource saturation occurs. Integrate with Console alerts and on-call runbooks.

Calibration and validation workflow:
- Offline: calibration jobs generate profiles and a validation set (representative prompts). Jobs produce baseline metrics and suggested thresholds.
- Pre-deploy: automated validation pipeline runs quantized kernels on the validation set and publishes a report (Confluence + dashboard) with per-layer sensitivity and recommended thresholds.
- Runtime: shadow-validation continuously compares live sample outputs; periodic aggregation is used to decide promotion.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Unit tests for comparator functions and metrics aggregation added and passing.
- Integration test that simulates shadow vs baseline disagreement and triggers promotion/rollback logic.
- End-to-end smoke on a canary model where promotion yields >=18% cost reduction and <0.5% end-user quality regression on held-out eval.
- Dashboard in Console with per-model shadow pass rate, top-k agreement trend, and latency impact.
- Runbook entry for rollback and on-call playbook completed.

Telemetry and metrics to collect:
- Shadow pass rate (per model, per route, per seq-len bucket)
- Top-k agreement, embedding cosine similarity, KL divergence
- p50/p95/p99 latency for both baseline and candidate path
- Memory/GPU utilization and failure rates for quant kernels
- Promotion events and rollback reasons

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: feature-flagged internal testing with synthetic traffic (this ticket covers implementation).
- Phase 1: limited internal canary (1% traffic) on non-critical customers with telemetry-only observation window for 24h.
- Phase 2: automated promotion to 5% then 20% if metrics hold across 48h windows.
- Phase 3: broad availability with Console controls and opt-outs.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Sampling: how to pick a representative shadow sample without overloading GPUs? We will start at 1% and adapt sampling by route.
- Metric thresholds: balancing sensitivity vs false positives. We'll tune thresholds via offline calibration suites.
- Storage cost for shadow outputs: keep only aggregated metrics and sample raw outputs for debugging.

Docs & artifacts:
- Calibration job spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/quant-calibration-job-spec
- Proposed policy schema: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345678

Implementation notes:
- Leverage existing kernel dispatch hook; add shadow execution path that shares KV cache when safe to reduce overhead.
- Reuse telemetry infra (metrics + traces) and extend with comparator metrics.
- Ensure shadow runs are low-priority and preempt safely under resource pressure.
